repository.name: camunda-bpmn-model
repository.description: BPMN model API written in Java - A library for reading and writing BPMN 2.0 XML files using a Java object model
repository.migration_note: Merged with camunda-bpm-platform project. Active development continues in camunda-bpm-platform repository under model-api/bpmn-model directory

conditions: Include original license and copyright notices
Provide copy of license to recipients
Include readable copy of NOTICE file attributions
license.assessment: Highly permissive open source license suitable for reuse in both open source and commercial projects. Patent grant provides additional protection. No copyleft requirements.

runtime.name: camunda-xml-model
runtime.description: Lightweight toolkit for implementing metamodels in Java - provides the base XML processing framework

build_plugins.purpose: Generates OSGi manifest with org.camunda.bpm.model* package exports

build_plugins.name: license-maven-plugin
build_plugins.purpose: License compliance checking, excludes test scope

jvm_dependencies: Java XML processing APIs (DOM, SAX, JAXP)

layers.name: Public API Layer
layers.description: Entry points and interfaces for client code
components: Bpmn.java - Main facade with static factory methods
Element interfaces (Process, Task, Event, Gateway, etc.)

layers.name: Builder Pattern Layer
layers.description: Fluent API for programmatic model creation
components: AbstractFlowNodeBuilder - Base for flow element builders
Concrete builders for each BPMN element type

layers.name: Model Implementation Layer
components: Uses delegation to xml-model base classes
Handles attribute and child element management

layers.name: Metamodel Registration Layer
components: Static registerType() methods in each implementation

layers.name: XML Processing Layer
layers.description: XML parsing, serialization, and DOM management
components: BpmnParser - XML schema validation and parsing

core_abstractions.name: Model
core_abstractions.description: Container for all type definitions and metamodel information

core_abstractions.name: ModelInstance

core_abstractions.name: ModelElementType
core_abstractions.description: Metamodel definition for each BPMN element type

core_abstractions.name: ModelElementInstance

metamodel_implementation.description: ModelElementType instances define the schema for element types at runtime, separating type metadata from instance data
metamodel_implementation.implementation: Static registerType() methods build ModelElementType using fluent builder API

metamodel_implementation.description: Each element implementation class registers its type definition in a static method called during model initialization
Fluent builder API for defining attributes, child elements, and sequences without imperative code

xml_binding.description: ModelElementInstance wraps DOM Element, delegating XML operations while providing typed API
benefits: Supports bidirectional sync between object model and XML

xml_binding.description: DOM elements are wrapped in ModelElementInstance only when accessed, with caching for subsequent access
xml_binding.implementation: ModelUtil.getModelElement() checks for cached instance before creating new wrapper

xml_binding.description: Attribute<T> objects encapsulate get/set operations on underlying DOM attributes with type conversion
Bidirectional references using ID/IDREF with automatic synchronization

builder_api.description: Builders use self-referential generics to enable fluent method chaining while preserving concrete type
builder_api.signature: public abstract class AbstractFlowNodeBuilder<B extends AbstractFlowNodeBuilder<B, E>, E extends FlowNode>
benefits: Return concrete builder type from each method

builder_api.description: Each builder provides methods to create and transition to builders for related elements
builder_api.example: serviceTask(), userTask(), exclusiveGateway() create elements and return appropriate builders

builder_api.description: Builders automatically create BpmnShape and BpmnEdge elements for visual layout
builder_api.implementation: createTarget() and createTargetBuilder() methods create both semantic and visual elements

model_api_design.description: Bpmn class provides static facade over complex initialization and parser APIs
Fluent API for filtering and retrieving elements from collections
AbstractModelParser defines parsing template with extension points for BPMN-specific behavior

validation.description: ModelElementValidator implementations visit elements during validation phase
ValidationResultCollector aggregates errors from multiple validators
benefits: Separates validation logic from result handling
Allows filtering and transformation of results

validation.description: Validators register for specific element types and automatically apply to instances and subtypes

extension_mechanism.description: Camunda extensions use separate XML namespace (http://camunda.org/schema/1.0/bpmn)
BPMN extensionElements container allows custom child elements

Bpmn.design: Singleton pattern with static facade, delegates to BpmnParser and internal methods

model_elements.coverage: Complete BPMN 2.0 specification including process, collaboration, choreography, and conversation elements

contents: Namespace URIs (BPMN20, BPMNDI, DC, DI, Camunda)
Element names for all BPMN types

levels: AbstractBaseElementBuilder - ID and basic element creation
Concrete builders for each element type (80+)

packages: bpmndi - BPMN Diagram Interchange (shapes, edges, diagrams)
diagram_support.integration: Builders automatically create and position diagram elements

type_registration.mechanism: Static registerType() method in each implementation class
type_registration.timing: Called during Model initialization via ModelBuilder

child_element_definition.sequence_builder: Defines ordering of child elements per XML schema

type_hierarchy.inheritance: Java inheritance mirrors BPMN type hierarchy
type_hierarchy.polymorphism: Queries and validators operate on base types and subtypes
type_hierarchy.extension: extendsType() establishes metamodel inheritance independent of Java inheritance

xml_schema_mapping.approach: Runtime metamodel with bidirectional XML binding

layers.purpose: Preserve exact XML structure for serialization
Wrap DOM elements with typed API

schema_validation.approach: W3C XML Schema validation during parsing
schema_validation.schema_location: Loaded from resources during BpmnParser initialization

evidence: Static registerType() methods manually define schema
No code generation plugins in pom.xml
No XSD-to-Java binding tools (e.g., JAXB) detected
code_generation.approach: Manual implementation with declarative type registration

pros: No dependency on code generation tools
cons: Slower to update for spec changes

patterns_instead_of_generation: Declarative type registration via fluent builders
Attribute and child element definitions in static methods

validation_approach.validator_registration: Validators register for specific element types and apply to all instances
validation_approach.extensibility: Custom validators can be added by implementing ModelElementValidator<T>

major_branches.name: FlowElement
major_branches.description: Elements that can be part of a process flow

factors.details: Implements complete BPMN 2.0 specification with 200+ element types
Runtime metamodel with declarative registration is sophisticated but well-designed
Recursive generics and 80+ builder classes add complexity but provide excellent API
Wrapper pattern with DOM delegation is straightforward once understood
Bidirectional references with automatic synchronization requires careful implementation
Namespace-based extensions are clean and well-separated

learning_curve.using_api: Low-Medium - Fluent builders and clear interfaces make usage straightforward
learning_curve.understanding_internals: High - Metamodel, type system, and DOM binding require significant study
learning_curve.extending: Medium-High - Adding new elements requires understanding type registration pattern

code_quality.organization: Excellent - Clear package structure, consistent naming
code_quality.documentation: Good - JavaDoc present, though examples could be more extensive
code_quality.consistency: Excellent - Patterns applied uniformly across all element types
code_quality.testability: Good - Clear separation of concerns, builder pattern aids testing

maintenance_burden.specification_updates: High - Manual updates required for BPMN spec changes
maintenance_burden.backward_compatibility: Good - Uses clirr-maven-plugin for API compatibility checking
maintenance_burden.extension: Medium - Adding new element types follows clear pattern

strengths: Excellent fluent builder API with type-safe method chaining
Clean separation of public API from implementation
Strong support for Camunda extensions via namespaces
Bidirectional sync between object model and XML
weaknesses: Archived repository - no active development in standalone repo
No code generation - all classes hand-written
Manual synchronization with BPMN specification required
Limited examples and documentation beyond JavaDoc
Recursive generics in builders can be confusing
DOM-based approach has memory overhead for large models
No streaming API for very large files
Tight coupling between semantic model and diagram info

for_reuse.rationale: Fluent API with recursive generics provides excellent developer experience
for_reuse.applicability: High - UML model construction would benefit from similar pattern

for_reuse.recommendation: Leverage the attribute and reference abstraction
for_reuse.rationale: Clean separation of typed accessors from DOM operations
for_reuse.applicability: High - UML has similar attribute and reference needs

for_reuse.recommendation: Consider separating semantic model from diagram information
for_reuse.rationale: Current tight coupling could be problematic for non-visual use cases
for_reuse.applicability: Medium - UML diagrams are separate concern from metamodel

for_reuse.recommendation: Evaluate code generation vs. manual implementation
for_reuse.rationale: Manual implementation gives control but increases maintenance
for_reuse.applicability: High - UML 2.5 is large specification, code generation might be beneficial

for_reuse.rationale: Clean way to add tool-specific extensions without polluting core model

architecture_lessons.description: Runtime metamodel separate from instances enables introspection
architecture_lessons.apply_to_uml: Essential for UML's reflective metamodel architecture

architecture_lessons.description: Preserves XML fidelity while providing clean API
architecture_lessons.apply_to_uml: Balance between XMI compatibility and usable API

architecture_lessons.description: Type registration via static methods called during initialization
architecture_lessons.apply_to_uml: Could work for UML but consider generated registration for large metamodel

implementation_guidance.camunda_approach: Declarative registration via fluent builders in static methods
implementation_guidance.for_uml: Consider code generation from UML metamodel XMI for consistency and maintainability

implementation_guidance.camunda_approach: Interface + Implementation + Builder for each element type
implementation_guidance.for_uml: Similar pattern appropriate, but consider partial builders given UML's size

implementation_guidance.camunda_approach: Wrapper pattern with lazy element wrapping and DOM delegation
implementation_guidance.for_uml: XMI has more complex requirements (XMI IDs, hrefs, etc.) but pattern is applicable
Map to UML profiles and stereotypes, plus tool-specific extensions
UML has more complex containment/reference semantics but pattern is sound

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Manual implementation becomes unmaintainable for UML's larger metamodel
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Invest in code generation from UML metamodel, use Camunda patterns as templates
Consider hybrid approach with streaming for large documents
Document pattern well, provide examples, consider simplified builders for common cases
Consider additional abstraction layer if alternative serializations needed (JSON, database, etc.)
